_README: Real 2026-27 seed data, researched from each school's official admissions pages (source_url) on last_verified. Requirements change every year: re-verify before relying on it, and read each school's "notes" for anything that could not be confirmed. Topics must come from server/src/topics.js. Re-running `npm run seed` updates schools by name without wiping users' data.

colleges.name: Brown University
colleges.notes: Prompts copied from Brown's official How to Apply page, which lists four required essays for the 2026-2027 cycle. The page gives word ranges, stored as the upper limit. Brown gives the deadlines as Nov 1 and Jan 5 with no year, so the years were inferred. The PLME and Brown|RISD Dual Degree essays are not listed. Brown also asks short Common App member questions (such as academic interests) that are not on the official essay page, so they are not listed. An optional video introduction exists. Interview availability was not verified, so no interview is listed. Testing has been required since 2024-25.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Open Curriculum essay
requirements.prompt_text: "There is something distinctive about Brown students. It is a blend of intellectual curiosity, creativity, and humility. A commitment to collaboration. An openness to new ideas and perspectives. A desire to make the world better. And it is resilience: the ability to recover and thrive after experiencing difficulties." From President Christina Paxson's 2025 Convocation Address. How will you use these characteristics or others to shape your approach to the Open Curriculum?

requirements.title: Growing up essay
requirements.prompt_text: Students entering Brown often find that making their home on College Hill naturally invites reflection on where they came from. Share how an aspect of your growing up has inspired or challenged you, and what unique contributions this might allow you to make to the Brown community.

requirements.title: Teach a class essay
requirements.prompt_text: If you could teach a class on any one thing, whether academic or otherwise, what would it be?

requirements.title: Something that brings you joy
requirements.prompt_text: Brown students care deeply about their work and the world around them. Students find contentment, satisfaction, and meaning in daily interactions and major discoveries. Whether big or small, mundane or spectacular, tell us about something that brings you joy.

colleges.name: California Institute of Technology
colleges.notes: Restrictive Early Action recorded as deadline_ea. Page is titled 'Fall 2027 Supplemental Application Essays'. STEM interest question also has a 150-word minimum and the Fun Question a 100-word minimum. Scientific Drive requires two essays on two different options (choose two of three), recorded as two requirements. The optional academic short answer has no published word limit. Recommendations: one STEM teacher and one humanities/social science teacher.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: STEM Academic Interest
requirements.prompt_text: If you had to choose an area of interest or two today, what would you choose? *Note that you are under no obligation to follow this choice if admitted. Why did you choose your proposed area of interest? If you selected 'other', what topics are you interested in pursuing?

requirements.title: Scholarly Character
requirements.prompt_text:
How do you learn when there is no easy answer? Caltech's learning environment asks students to work through difficulty, collaborate around hard ideas, and contribute to one another's understanding. Use these responses to show us how you learn and grow. Choose one of the following prompts:
Option 1 -- COLLABORATION: STEM as shared learning. Tell us about a time your learning in STEM was shaped by another person or group — either because you needed help, offered help, changed your thinking through collaboration, or contributed to someone else's understanding. What did that experience teach you about learning and working with others?
Option 2 -- PROCESS: The thought behind the outcome. Tell us about a time your approach to a STEM problem, concept, or project mattered as much as the outcome. How did you work through uncertainty or persist creatively in tackling the problem? What would you still defend about your process, regardless of the outcome?

requirements.title: Scientific Drive Essay 1
requirements.prompt_text:
How does STEM come alive in your life through learning, pursuing, or making? Caltech faculty review applications, so feel free to get technical in your response! Choose two of the following prompts (this is the first of your two):
Option 1 -- LEARNING: STEM as a never-ending rabbit hole. Regardless of your STEM interest listed above, take this opportunity to nerd out and talk to us about whatever STEM rabbit hole you have found yourself falling into. Be as specific or broad as you would like.
Option 2 -- PURSUING: STEM as sustained intellectual engagement. Tell us about a STEM question, problem, idea, or project that has held your attention over time. What drew you to it, how have you pursued it, and what do you still want to understand?
Option 3 -- MAKING: STEM as creation. Tell us about something you created, tested, repaired, modeled, coded, built, or redesigned. What problem were you trying to solve and what did the process reveal to you?

requirements.title: Scientific Drive Essay 2
requirements.prompt_text:
How does STEM come alive in your life through learning, pursuing, or making? Caltech faculty review applications, so feel free to get technical in your response! Choose two of the following prompts (this is the second of your two; pick a different option than Essay 1):
Option 1 -- LEARNING: STEM as a never-ending rabbit hole. Regardless of your STEM interest listed above, take this opportunity to nerd out and talk to us about whatever STEM rabbit hole you have found yourself falling into. Be as specific or broad as you would like.
Option 2 -- PURSUING: STEM as sustained intellectual engagement. Tell us about a STEM question, problem, idea, or project that has held your attention over time. What drew you to it, how have you pursued it, and what do you still want to understand?
Option 3 -- MAKING: STEM as creation. Tell us about something you created, tested, repaired, modeled, coded, built, or redesigned. What problem were you trying to solve and what did the process reveal to you?

requirements.title: Fun Question
requirements.prompt_text: Caltech students bring more than academic ability to the communities they join. What is something you would be excited to do, share, teach, make, start, or contribute as part of the Caltech community?

requirements.title: Optional Academic Short Answer
requirements.prompt_text: Caltech cares about context. Is there anything about your academic preparation, coursework, school context, or learning experiences that would help us better understand your readiness for Caltech?

colleges.name: Carnegie Mellon University
colleges.notes: The page gives deadlines without years ('November 2', 'January 4'); the years are inferred (Nov 1, 2026 is a Sunday). CMU does not label its short-answer page with a cycle year, so these may be carried over from 2025-26. Each short answer is capped at 300 words. CMU has no per-college essays; applicants to more than one college should cover all their interests in the short answers. Testing varies by program: SAT/ACT required for the School of Computer Science, 'test flexible' (some test required) for most colleges, optional for Fine Arts. Drama and Music have a 2026-12-01 RD deadline and no ED. Fine Arts requires a portfolio or audition.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Short Answer 1: Passion for Area of Study
requirements.prompt_text: Most students choose their intended major or area of study based on a passion or inspiration that’s developed over time — what passion or inspiration led you to choose this area of study?

requirements.title: Short Answer 2: Successful College Experience
requirements.prompt_text: Many students pursue college for a specific degree, career opportunity or personal goal. Whichever it may be, learning will be critical to achieve your ultimate goal. As you think ahead to the process of learning during your college years, how will you define a successful college experience?

requirements.title: Short Answer 3: What to Emphasize
requirements.prompt_text: Consider your application as a whole. What do you personally want to emphasize about your application for the admission committee’s consideration? Highlight something that’s important to you or something you haven’t had a chance to share. Tell us, don’t show us (no websites please).

colleges.name: Columbia University
colleges.notes: Prompts copied from Columbia's official Columbia-Specific Application Questions page (updated July 28, 2026). The ED date (Nov 1) is confirmed for Fall 2027. Columbia lists the RD date as January 1 but warns that its dates follow a typical cycle. Columbia is test-optional for the 2026-27 cycle and will require testing from 2027-28. Columbia does not offer interviews. Columbia also accepts the Coalition App on Scoir.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: List: Texts and resources for intellectual development
requirements.prompt_text: List the titles of texts, resources and outlets that have contributed to your intellectual development outside of academic courses, including but not limited to books, journals, websites, podcasts, essays, plays, presentations, videos, museums and other content that you enjoy.

requirements.title: Short answer: Lived experience
requirements.prompt_text: Tell us about an aspect of your life so far or your lived experience that is important to you, and describe how it has shaped the way you would learn from and contribute to Columbia's multidimensional and collaborative environment.

requirements.title: Short answer: A time you did not agree
requirements.prompt_text: At Columbia, students representing a wide range of perspectives are invited to live and learn together. In such a community, questions and debates naturally arise. Please describe a time when you did not agree with someone and discuss how you engaged with them and what you took away from the interaction.

requirements.title: Short answer: Navigating adversity
requirements.prompt_text: In college/university, students are often challenged in ways that they could not anticipate. Please describe a situation in which you have navigated through adversity and discuss how you changed as a result.

requirements.title: Short answer: Why Columbia
requirements.prompt_text: Why are you interested in attending Columbia University? We encourage you to consider the aspect(s) that you find unique and compelling about Columbia.

requirements.title: Short answer: Preferred areas of study
requirements.prompt_text: What attracts you to your preferred areas of study at Columbia College or Columbia Engineering?

colleges.name: Cornell University
colleges.notes: Cornell has NO university-wide essay prompt for the 2026-27 cycle (the official supplement page lists only college/school-specific essays), so none is included. Applicants answer only the prompts for the one college they apply to; only Arts & Sciences and Duffield Engineering are included here, so all college prompts are marked optional. Engineering prompts from https://admissions.cornell.edu/first-year-duffield-engineering-applicants. Cornell pages do not state the cycle year explicitly but appear current. Dates are from the official first-year page (ED Nov 1, RD Jan 2).

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: College of Arts and Sciences Essay
requirements.prompt_text: At the College of Arts and Sciences, your education is yours to shape. Describe an intellectual passion, question, or idea that has captured your attention—whether it emerges from your studies or extends beyond your coursework. What specific aspects of our liberal arts curriculum would you draw on to explore and connect your varied interests?

requirements.title: College of Engineering Long Essay 1
requirements.prompt_text: Fundamentally, engineering is the application of math, science, and technology to solve complex problems. Why do you want to study engineering?

requirements.title: College of Engineering Long Essay 2
requirements.prompt_text: Why do you think you would love to study at Duffield Engineering?

requirements.title: College of Engineering Short Answer 1
requirements.prompt_text: What brings you joy?

requirements.title: College of Engineering Short Answer 2
requirements.prompt_text: What do you believe you will contribute to the Duffield Engineering community beyond what you've already detailed in your application? What unique voice will you bring?

requirements.title: College of Engineering Short Answer 3
requirements.prompt_text: What is one activity, club, team, organization, work/volunteer experience or family responsibility that is especially meaningful to you? Please briefly tell us about its significance for you.

requirements.title: College of Engineering Short Answer 4
requirements.prompt_text: What is one award you have received or achievement you have attained that has meant the most to you? Please briefly describe its importance to you.

colleges.name: Dartmouth College
colleges.notes: Prompts copied from Dartmouth's official writing supplement page for the Class of 2031 (updated July 22, 2026). Dartmouth's apply page gives two different RD deadlines: the timeline says January 1, while the QuestBridge section says January 2. January 1 is used here. The $85 first-year fee is from Dartmouth's glossary page. The peer recommendation is optional. The alumni interview is optional and invitation-based. Testing (SAT or ACT) is required.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Why Dartmouth
requirements.prompt_text: As you seek admission to Dartmouth's Class of 2031, what aspects of the college's academic program, community, and/or campus environment attract your interest? How is Dartmouth a good fit for you?

requirements.title: Introduce yourself (choose one)
requirements.prompt_text: Respond to one of the following prompts: A. There is a Quaker saying: Let your life speak. Describe the environment in which you were raised and the impact it has had on the person you are today. B. "Be yourself," Oscar Wilde advised. "Everyone else is taken." Introduce yourself.

requirements.title: Second essay (choose one)
requirements.prompt_text: Respond to one of the following prompts: A. What excites you? B. Labor leader and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta recommended a life of purpose. "We must use our lives to make the world a better place to live, not just to acquire things," she said. "That is what we are put on the earth for." In what ways do you hope to make—or are you already making—an impact? Why? How? C. In an Instagram post, best-selling British author Matt Haig cheered the impact of reading. "A good novel is the best invention humans have ever created for imagining other lives," he wrote. How have you experienced such insight from reading? What did you read and how did it alter the way you understand yourself and others? D. The social and family interactions of wild chimpanzees have been the focus of Dame Jane Goodall's research for decades. Her understanding of animal behavior prompted the English primatologist to see a lesson for human communities as well: "Change happens by listening and then starting a dialogue with the people who are doing something you don't believe is right." Channel Dame Goodall: Tell us about a moment when you engaged in a difficult conversation or encountered someone with an opinion or perspective that was different from your own. How did you find common ground? E. Celebrate your nerdy side. F. "It's not easy being green…" was the frequent refrain of Kermit the Frog. How has difference been a part of your life, and how have you embraced it as part of your identity, outlook, or sense of purpose?

colleges.name: Duke University
colleges.notes: Deadlines shown on the official page as Nov 2 (ED) and Jan 4 (RD) without years; assumed 2026/2027. Test-optional for 2026-27. The optional Duke Embark 150-word response is not included because its prompt text is not published on the admissions page. Alumni interviews are offered at Duke's discretion; Glimpse video is optional for US students.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Why Duke
requirements.prompt_text: What is your impression of Duke as a university and community, and why do you believe it is a good match for your goals, values, and interests? If there is something specific that attracts you to our academic offerings in Trinity College of Arts and Sciences or the Pratt School of Engineering, or to our co-curricular opportunities, feel free to include that, too.

requirements.title: Communities
requirements.prompt_text: We all belong to communities defined by place, faith, family, culture, interests or shared experience. Tell us about a community that has shaped who you are, any way it has set you apart, and what you’ve learned from being part of it that you hope to bring to Duke.

requirements.title: Optional Short Essay
requirements.prompt_text:
We want to emphasize that the following questions are optional. We invite you to answer one of the three if you believe that doing so will add something meaningful that is not already addressed elsewhere in your application.
Viewpoints and experiences: We believe a wide range of viewpoints and experiences is essential to maintaining Duke’s vibrant living and learning community. Please share anything in this context that might help us better understand you and your potential contributions to Duke.
Difference of opinion: Meaningful dialogue often involves respectful disagreement. Provide an example of a difference of opinion you’ve had with someone you care about. What did you learn from it?
Something you are excited about: What’s the last thing that you’ve been really excited about?

colleges.name: Emory University
colleges.notes: ED II deadline is Jan 1 (ED I used). The official deadlines page lists month and day only, and the year is inferred. The 200-word academic-interests limit is a 'recommended length'. Emory requires two teacher evaluations from core academic teachers; the counselor school report is assumed through Common App.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Academic Interests
requirements.prompt_text: What academic areas are you interested in exploring at Emory University and why?

requirements.title: Getting to Know You
requirements.prompt_text: Answer one of the following questions: (1) Emory University has a strong commitment to building community. Tell us about a community that you have been part of where your personal participation helped to change or shape the community for the better. (2) Reflect on a personal experience where you intentionally expanded your cultural awareness. (3) Emory University’s unique mission calls for service to humanity. Share how you might personally contribute to this mission of service to humanity. (4) In a scholarly community, differing ideas often collide before they converge. How do you personally navigate disagreement in a way that promotes progress and deepens meaningful dialogue?

colleges.name: Georgetown University
colleges.notes: Applicants can use the Georgetown Application or the Common App; platform is set to 'own' because Georgetown does NOT require the Common App Personal Statement (its own 650-word Essay 1 replaces it, and the Common App essay may be reused there), so the shared Common App essay is left out. The page gives deadlines without years; years are inferred for this cycle. The school-specific essay is REQUIRED, but its prompt depends on the school applied to; only 2 of 7 schools are listed (College of Arts & Sciences, Walsh SFS) and marked optional per seed convention. The others are McCourt Public Policy, Earth Commons, Nursing, School of Health and McDonough Business. The $80 fee comes from Georgetown's own application page. An alumni interview is required when one is assigned.

requirements.title: Short Essay 1: Most Involved Activity
requirements.prompt_text: Briefly discuss the significance to you of the school or summer activity in which you have been most involved.

requirements.title: Short Essay 2: Different Viewpoints
requirements.prompt_text: In all our lives, we interact with people who hold different viewpoints than our own. Describe such an event you experienced. What did you learn from the experience?

requirements.title: Essay 1: Personal or Creative Essay
requirements.prompt_text: As Georgetown is a diverse community, the Admissions Committee would like to know more about you in your own words. Please submit a brief personal or creative essay which you feel best describes you and reflects on your personal background and individual experiences, skills, and talents.

requirements.title: Essay 2: College of Arts & Sciences
requirements.prompt_text: Founded in 1789, the Georgetown College of Arts & Sciences is committed to the Jesuit traditions of an integrated education and of productive research in the natural sciences, humanities, social sciences, and fine arts. Describe your interest in studying in the College of Arts & Sciences. Applicants interested in the sciences, mathematics, or languages are encouraged to make specific reference to their choice of major.

requirements.title: Essay 2: Walsh School of Foreign Service
requirements.prompt_text: Georgetown University’s Walsh School of Foreign Service was founded more than a century ago to prepare generations of leaders with the foundational skills to address global issues. Describe your primary motivations for studying international affairs at Georgetown University and dedicating your undergraduate studies toward a future in global service.

colleges.name: Georgia Institute of Technology
colleges.notes: Early Action 1 (Oct 15) is for Georgia students; Early Action 2 (Nov 2) is for non-Georgia students. EA1 is used here. Years are inferred from the '2026-2027 Important Dates' table. Georgia Tech dropped its 'why major' supplement for 2026-27; the official essays page lists only the Common App prompts. SAT/ACT scores are required. Recommendations are not listed as part of a complete application and appear optional. The fee is $85 for international applicants.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

colleges.name: Harvard University
colleges.notes: Prompts copied from Harvard's official 2026-2027 First Year Application Supplement (valid for Fall 2027 entrance). Early round is Restrictive Early Action. Fee of $95 taken from college.harvard.edu/admissions/apply (third-party sites list $85). Harvard also accepts the Coalition App. Alumni interview is offered when available and is not required.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Short answer: Contributing to Harvard
requirements.prompt_text: Harvard has long recognized the importance of enrolling a student body with a diversity of perspectives and experiences. How will the life experiences that shaped who you are today enable you to contribute to Harvard?

requirements.title: Short answer: A time you disagreed
requirements.prompt_text: Describe a time when you strongly disagreed with someone about an idea or issue. How did you communicate or engage with this person? What did you learn from this experience?

requirements.title: Short answer: Activities that shaped you
requirements.prompt_text: Briefly describe any of your extracurricular activities, employment experience, travel, or family responsibilities that have shaped who you are.

requirements.title: Short answer: Using your Harvard education
requirements.prompt_text: How do you hope to use your Harvard education in the future?

requirements.title: Short answer: Top 3 things for roommates
requirements.prompt_text: Top 3 things your roommates might like to know about you.

colleges.name: Johns Hopkins University
colleges.notes: ED II deadline is 2027-01-02 (same as RD). Coalition on Scoir also accepted. JHU does not list interviews. Prompt text was read through a summarizing fetch tool (direct download blocked), so it was assembled from quoted fragments of the official 2026-27 Hopkins Insider post and matched against a third-party copy.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Hopkins Supplemental Essay
requirements.prompt_text: At Johns Hopkins, community is built through dialogue, collaboration, and a willingness to engage across differences. Whether on campus or in the broader world, community depends on bridge builders who can listen to differing perspectives, challenge their own assumptions, or work together toward shared goals. Drawing on your own experiences, what have you learned about engaging across differences and how has it shaped the way you think about building bridges, enhancing community, and working with others?

colleges.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
colleges.notes: MIT uses its own application (no Common App personal essay). MIT gives approximate lengths ('approximately 100–200 words' for main essays, '40 to 50 words' for short responses) rather than hard limits; recorded as 200 and 50. Dates from https://mitadmissions.org/apply/firstyear/deadlines-requirements/ (year inferred as Nov 1, 2026 / Jan 4, 2027). The final open-ended additional-information box has no fixed prompt text and is omitted. Interview is offered if an Educational Counselor is available.

requirements.title: Field of Study
requirements.prompt_text: What field of study appeals to you the most right now? (Note: Applicants select from a drop-down list.) Reflect on what has led you to this interest.

requirements.title: Different Than Expected
requirements.prompt_text: While some reach their goals following well-trodden paths, others blaze their own trails achieving the unexpected. In what ways have you done something different than what was expected in your educational journey?

requirements.title: Problems to Tackle
requirements.prompt_text: How have your personal and academic experiences influenced the types of problems you would want to tackle with an MIT education and the impact you aim to make on your community?

requirements.title: Unexpected Challenge
requirements.prompt_text: How did you manage a situation or challenge that you didn’t expect? What did you learn from it?

requirements.title: Short Response: Just for Fun
requirements.prompt_text: What do you do just for fun?

requirements.title: Short Response: Someone You Admire
requirements.prompt_text: Who is someone you admire, whether you know them personally or look up to them from afar? Tell us why.

requirements.title: Short Response: Topic for Hours
requirements.prompt_text: What’s a topic, academic or non-academic, that you could talk about for hours?

requirements.title: Short Response: Generalist or Specialist
requirements.prompt_text: MIT values both “generalists” with varied interests and “specialists” who focus deeply on one or a few passions. Which do you think best describes you, and why?

colleges.name: New York University
colleges.notes: ED II deadline is 2027-01-01 (ED I used). Deadlines are from secondary sources, not confirmed on nyu.edu (page wouldn't load). Supplement prompt text came from MEET NYU (official) in excerpts and was put back together. The 250-word limit is not on NYU's page and comes from third-party guides. The $85 fee comes from NYU and NYU Abu Dhabi fee pages, which may be dated. NYU says it is test-optional through 2027-28 (NYU Abu Dhabi page). NYU asks for one letter of recommendation (teacher or other) plus the counselor's school report. Tisch/Steinhardt artistic programs require a portfolio or audition.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: NYU Bridge Builder Essay
requirements.prompt_text: We are looking for students who want to be bridge builders—students who can connect people, groups, and ideas to span divides, foster understanding, and promote collaboration within a dynamic, interconnected, and vibrant global academic community. We are eager for you to tell us how your experiences have helped you understand what qualities and efforts are needed to bridge divides so that people can better learn and work together. Please consider one or more of the following questions in your essay: Tell us about a time you encountered a perspective different from your own. What did you learn—about yourself, the other person, or the world? Tell us about an experience you’ve had working with others who have different perspectives. What role did you try to play in helping people to work together, and what did you learn from your efforts? Tell us about someone you’ve observed who does a particularly good job helping people think or work together. How does this person set the stage for common exploration or work? How do they react when challenges arise? What qualities do you admire in this person?

colleges.name: Northwestern University
colleges.notes: Northwestern no longer requires the Common App personal essay for 2026-27 (it is welcomed but optional), so it is marked optional:true. Applicants may answer 0–2 of the five optional short answers (encouraged to answer at least one), recorded as two optional requirements each listing all choices; limit is 'fewer than 200 words'. Also accepts Coalition with Scoir. Test-optional. Requires one counselor and one teacher recommendation. No alumni interviews; Glimpse video optional for US applicants. Bienen (music) applicants have additional audition requirements not included.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Background and Engagement
requirements.prompt_text: We want to be sure we’re considering your application in the context of your personal experiences: What aspects of your background (your identity, your school setting, your community, your household, etc.) have most shaped how you see yourself engaging in Northwestern’s community, be it academically, extracurricularly, culturally, politically, socially, or otherwise?

requirements.title: Optional Short Answer 1
requirements.prompt_text:
We encourage you to answer at least one and no more than two of the following questions:
Painting “The Rock” is a tradition at Northwestern that invites all forms of expression—students promote campus events or extracurricular groups, support social or activist causes, show their Wildcat spirit (what we call “Purple Pride”), celebrate their culture, and more. What would you paint on The Rock, and why?
Northwestern fosters a distinctively interdisciplinary culture. We believe discovery and innovation thrive at the intersection of diverse ideas, perspectives, and academic interests. Within this setting, if you could dream up an undergraduate class, research project, or creative effort (a start-up, a design prototype, a performance, etc.), what would it be? Who might be some ideal classmates or collaborators?
Community and belonging matter at Northwestern. Tell us about one or more communities, networks, or student groups you see yourself connecting with on campus.
Northwestern’s location is special: on the shore of Lake Michigan, steps from downtown Evanston, just a few miles from Chicago. What aspects of our location are most compelling to you, and why?
Northwestern is a place where people with diverse backgrounds from all over the world can study, live, and talk with one another. This range of experiences and viewpoints immeasurably enriches learning. How might your individual background contribute to this diversity of perspectives in Northwestern’s classrooms and around our campus?

requirements.title: Optional Short Answer 2
requirements.prompt_text:
We encourage you to answer at least one and no more than two of the following questions (choose a different one than Optional Short Answer 1):
Painting “The Rock” is a tradition at Northwestern that invites all forms of expression—students promote campus events or extracurricular groups, support social or activist causes, show their Wildcat spirit (what we call “Purple Pride”), celebrate their culture, and more. What would you paint on The Rock, and why?
Northwestern fosters a distinctively interdisciplinary culture. We believe discovery and innovation thrive at the intersection of diverse ideas, perspectives, and academic interests. Within this setting, if you could dream up an undergraduate class, research project, or creative effort (a start-up, a design prototype, a performance, etc.), what would it be? Who might be some ideal classmates or collaborators?
Community and belonging matter at Northwestern. Tell us about one or more communities, networks, or student groups you see yourself connecting with on campus.
Northwestern’s location is special: on the shore of Lake Michigan, steps from downtown Evanston, just a few miles from Chicago. What aspects of our location are most compelling to you, and why?
Northwestern is a place where people with diverse backgrounds from all over the world can study, live, and talk with one another. This range of experiences and viewpoints immeasurably enriches learning. How might your individual background contribute to this diversity of perspectives in Northwestern’s classrooms and around our campus?

colleges.name: Princeton University
colleges.notes: Prompts copied from Princeton's official 'Princeton-specific Questions' page for the 2026-27 cycle. Early round is Single-Choice Early Action. Princeton gives the deadlines as Nov. 1 and Jan. 1 with no year, so the years were inferred. Princeton is test-optional for fall 2027 entry and will require testing again for fall 2028. 'Your Voice' is 400-500 words, so the limit is stored as 500. The graded written paper is stored as type 'portfolio' because there is no better type. The $75 fee is NOT confirmed on Princeton's own site and comes from third-party sources. The alumni interview is optional and offered when available. The Optional Arts Supplement is due Nov 6 for SCEA applicants.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay

requirements.title: Academic interests (A.B. or B.S.E.)
requirements.prompt_text: Answer the prompt for your intended degree. For A.B. Degree Applicants or Those Who Are Undecided: As a research institution that also prides itself on its liberal arts curriculum, Princeton allows students to explore areas across the humanities and the arts, the natural sciences, and the social sciences. requirements.title: More About You: What brings you joy
requirements.prompt_text: What brings you joy?

colleges.notes: ED II deadline is 2027-01-04 (same as RD). The page gives deadlines without years ('November 1', 'January 4'); the years are inferred from the 2026-2027 essay heading. requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay

requirements.title: Academic Interests

requirements.title: Why Rice

requirements.title: Rice Community Contribution (choose one)
requirements.prompt_text:
Please respond to one of the following prompts to explore how you will contribute to the Rice community:
1. The Residential College System is at the heart of Rice student life and is heavily influenced by the particular cultural traditions and unique life experiences each student brings. What life experiences and/or unique perspectives are you looking forward to sharing with fellow Owls in the residential college system?
2. Rice is strengthened by its diverse community of learning and discovery that produces leaders and change agents across the spectrum of human endeavor. What perspectives shaped by your background, experiences, upbringing, and/or cultural identity inspire you to join our community of change agents at Rice?

requirements.title: Architecture: Compelling Place
requirements.prompt_text: Describe a building, place, or city that you have encountered and found especially compelling. What specifically captured your attention, and why? In your response, reflect on how this experience has shaped your understanding of architecture and the built environment.

colleges.name: University of California, Berkeley

requirements.title: PIQ 7: Community

colleges.name: University of Chicago
colleges.notes: ED I and EA both due Nov 2, 2026; ED II and RD due Jan 4, 2027 (from the official application page). Also accepts Coalition with Scoir. UChicago publishes no word limits for its essays, so word_limit is null. 'No Harm' testing policy (test-optional). Fee is $90 but waived for students applying for need-based aid. The 2-minute video profile is optional/recommended and is not an interview.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Question 1: Why UChicago
requirements.prompt_text: How does the University of Chicago, as you know it now, satisfy your desire for a particular kind of learning, community, and future? Please address with some specificity your own wishes and how they relate to UChicago.

requirements.title: Question 2: Extended Essay
requirements.prompt_text:
Choose one of the following:
Essay Option 1: Food for thought: How do thoughts eat? (Inspired by Ernest Leong, Class of 2026)
Essay Option 2: The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, utilized origami-inspired techniques to compactly store and deploy its sunshield in space. Choose an artistic practice and use its principles to propose an elegant solution to a problem. (Inspired by Akhil Korra, Class of 2028)
Essay Option 3: Sometimes metaphors get mixed up. For one reason or another, one could say, “we'll burn that bridge when we get there” or “the world is your china shop”. Make up your own mixed metaphor. Explain how it could make sense, be understood, or even applied. (Inspired by Julia Nieberg, Class of 2029)
Essay Option 4: The Olympics have long celebrated the pinnacle of human athletic achievement. But what if they expanded to honor the mundane? Imagine a new Olympic event built around an everyday activity like speed dishwashing or competitive grocery bagging. How is it scored, officiated, and judged? Why is it a worthy addition? (Inspired by Ewan Smith, Class of 2028)
Essay Option 5: AI: Allen Iverson. NASA, or the North American Saxophone Alliance. Share a potentially confounding, comedic, or captivating example of MIA (Mistaken Identity of Acronym) and tell us its backstory. (Inspired by Jeeho Byun, Class of 2030)
Essay Option 6: And, as always… the classic choose your own adventure option! In the spirit of adventurous inquiry, choose one of our past prompts (or create a question of your own). Be original, creative, thought provoking. Draw on your best qualities as a writer, thinker, visionary, social critic, sage, citizen of the world, or future citizen of the University of Chicago; take a little risk, and have fun!

Honors Program and Innovation Academy have additional optional essays (text not verified). UF does not accept letters of recommendation. Test scores (SAT/ACT/CLT) are required for Florida public universities; UF page describes self-reporting/submitting them and a materials deadline, not marked optional. Academic record is via STARS (self-reported); official final transcript due after admission.

colleges.name: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

Declared applicants answer the two first-choice major prompts; Undeclared applicants answer the two alternative prompts instead (both versions are in each requirement's prompt_text). Second-choice essay only if a second-choice major is selected. Deadlines from official first-year page (EA Nov 1, RD Jan 5) shown without year; assumed 2026-27 cycle. requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Illinois essay 1: Major experience
requirements.prompt_text: First-choice major applicants: Explain, in detail, an experience you've had in the past 3 to 4 years related to your first-choice major. This can be an experience from an extracurricular activity, in a class you've taken, or through something else. | Undeclared applicants instead: What are your future career or academic goals? You may include courses you took in high school and how these impacted your goals.

requirements.title: Illinois essay 2: Goals and interests
requirements.prompt_text: First-choice major applicants: Describe your personal and/or career goals after graduating from Illinois and how your selected first-choice major will help you achieve them. | Undeclared applicants instead: What are your academic interests? Please include 2-3 majors you're considering at Illinois and why.

requirements.title: Second-choice major essay

colleges.notes: admissions.umich.edu blocked automated access (403). U-M's help-desk KB confirmed the essay structure and limits (two U-M essays of 100-300 and 100-550 words). U-M stays test-optional for the 2027 cycle (U-M Application Changes page). The $75 fee and counselor + one teacher recs come from older U-M pages. U-M also has an optional essay on the impact of challenges, but its exact wording was not found, so it is left out. SMTD (RD-only, Dec 1) and Stamps require portfolios or auditions.

In your essay, share with us how you are prepared to contribute to these goals. This could include the people, places, experiences, or aspirations that have shaped your journey and future plans.

Test scores are optional for applicants with a weighted GPA of 2.8 or higher; below that, an ACT of 17+ or SAT of 930+ is required. One teacher rec from a core subject is required. The counselor school report is part of Common App; the page does not mention a counselor letter.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

colleges.name: University of Notre Dame
colleges.notes: Early round is Restrictive Early Action. The page gives deadlines without years; the years are inferred because the page describes the 2026-2027 testing policy. Short answers must be 50-100 words each; the limit is stored as 100. Coalition also accepted. Tests are optional through 2026-27 and required again from the 2027-28 cycle. The second recommendation should come from the counselor if possible (another recommender is allowed). Notre Dame does not interview.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Non-Negotiable Factor Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Everyone has different priorities when considering their higher education options and building their college or university list. Tell us about your “non-negotiable” factor(s) when searching for your future college home.

requirements.title: Short Answers (choose two)
requirements.prompt_text:
Please choose two questions from the options below. Your response to each short-answer question should be between 50-100 words.
1. How does faith influence the decisions you make?
2. What is distinctive about your personal experiences and development (eg, family support, culture, disability, personal background, community)? Why are these experiences important to you and how will you enrich the Notre Dame community?
3. Notre Dame’s undergraduate experience is characterized by a collective sense of care for every person. How do you foster service to others in your community?
4. What would you fight for?

colleges.name: University of Pennsylvania
colleges.notes: Prompts copied from Penn's official 2026-27 Short Answer and Essay Prompts page. Each prompt is 50-200 words, stored as 200. The school-specific prompt depends on which of the four undergraduate schools you apply to, so all four are stored as one requirement. Extra essays for coordinated dual-degree and specialized programs (Huntsman, LSM, M&T, NHCM, VIPER, and others) are not listed. Penn requires one counselor letter and one core-subject teacher letter, and accepts an optional second letter from a teacher or other supporter. Testing is required, with a hardship waiver available. Alumni interviews are optional and depend on availability (not verified on a Penn page this session). Penn also accepts the Coalition App and QuestBridge.

requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Thank-you note
requirements.prompt_text: Write a short thank-you note to someone you have not yet thanked and would like to acknowledge. (We encourage you to share this note with that person, if possible, and reflect on the experience!)

requirements.title: Exploring community at Penn
requirements.prompt_text: How will you explore community at Penn? Consider how Penn will help shape your perspective, and how your experiences and perspective will help shape Penn.

requirements.title: Undergraduate school-specific prompt
requirements.prompt_text: Answer the prompt for the undergraduate school you are applying to. School of Nursing: Penn Nursing intends to meet the health needs of society in a global and multicultural world by preparing its students to impact healthcare by advancing science. Why are you applying to Nursing, where do you see yourself professionally in the future, and how will you contribute to our mission of promoting equity in healthcare? College of Arts and Sciences: The College of Arts and Sciences is designed to foster discovery and connection. Describe something you are curious about—something you'd like to learn more about or find a new approach to—and how you might pursue that curiosity in the College. The Wharton School: Wharton prepares its students to make an impact by applying business methods and economic theory to real-world problems, including economic, political, and social issues. Discuss a current issue of importance to you and how you hope a Wharton education would help you explore it. Penn Engineering: Penn Engineering prepares its students to become leaders in technology by combining a strong foundation in the natural sciences and mathematics with depth of study in focused disciplinary majors. Describe how you plan to pursue your engineering interests at Penn, particularly within the intended major you selected.

Short takes have a 200-character limit, which Yale itself calls approximately 35 words. The academic-interest question (pick up to three areas from a list) is a selection, not an essay, so it is not listed. The $80 fee is NOT confirmed on Yale's own site and comes from third-party sources. The alumni interview depends on availability. Optional arts and research supplements are accepted. Coalition and QuestBridge are also accepted.

requirements.title: Common App Personal Essay
requirements.prompt_text: Choose one of the seven Common App prompts and write a personal essay of up to 650 words.

requirements.title: Short answer: Topic or idea that excites you
requirements.prompt_text: Tell us about a topic or idea that excites you and is related to one or more academic areas you selected above. Why are you drawn to it?

requirements.title: Short take: Course, book, or art you would create
requirements.prompt_text: If you could teach any college course, write a book, or create an original piece of art of any kind, what would it be?

requirements.title: Short take: Aspect to grow in college
requirements.prompt_text: What is one aspect of yourself that you hope to grow or develop during college?

requirements.title: Short take: Something not elsewhere in your application
requirements.prompt_text: What is something about you that is not included anywhere else in your application?

requirements.title: Yale Essay (choose one)
requirements.prompt_text: Respond to one of the following prompts: (1) Reflect on a time you discussed an issue important to you with someone holding an opposing view. Why did you find the experience meaningful? (2) Reflect on your membership in a community to which you feel connected. Why is this community meaningful to you? You may define community however you like. (3) Reflect on an element of your personal experience that you feel will enrich your college. How has it shaped you?
